description.value: A fast event-related fMRI study examined smoking-cue effects during an attention-demanding emotion recognition task in smokers and matched non-smokers, including associations with smoking dependence.

spans.text: Thirteen tobacco smokers and a demographically matched group of 13 healthy non-smokers participated in a fast event-related functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study that involved a visual task integrating SCs and neutral cues (NCs) during emotion recognition trials requiring a high level of attention.

value: functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) could reveal differential effects of SCs versus NCs in smokers'—but not in non-smokers'—prefrontal, limbic, paralimbic and striatal areas
We also expected higher error rates and longer reaction times in smokers than controls, consistent with an SC-induced attentional bias.

description.value: An observational, cross-sectional study of healthy smokers and never-smoked healthy volunteers, with no intervention allocation and one imaging visit.

spans.text: The statistical parametric maps of the SCs minus NCs contrast ([SCs − NCs]) obtained for each participant were entered in a second-level one-way ANOVA, including the group (smokers and non-smokers) as the between-subject factor.
The order of task presentation was counterbalanced across subjects.

value: In smokers, the SCs minus NCs comparison revealed increased activity in one cluster in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
This activation may reflect an adaptive top-down process involving the right lateral prefrontal cortex, enabling smokers to inhibit cue-induced craving during the attention-demanding task.
In smokers, a decreased activity was found in a set of areas, including most of the limbic and paralimbic regions and the striatum.
The observed changes could mainly reflect inhibition of cue-induced craving rather than craving itself.

definition.value: SCs minus NCs in smokers compared with non-smokers, showing hypoactivation in smokers

value: Group analysis confirmed that some limbic and paralimbic regions were less activated in smokers than in non-smokers for the SCs minus NCs comparison.
These findings suggest that smokers can modify their neural reactivity to smoking cues when executing an attention-demanding task.

name.value: Area showing hyperactivation in smokers in comparison to non-smokers

definition.value: SCs minus NCs in smokers compared with non-smokers, showing hyperactivation in smokers

value: Group analysis confirmed that the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex was more activated in smokers than in non-smokers for the SCs minus NCs comparison.
This may reflect an adaptive top-down process involving right lateral prefrontal activation and successful inhibition of cue-induced craving.

value: There was a negative correlation in smokers between the Fagerström score and the SCs minus NCs comparison in the right insula: the higher the FTND score, the lower the right insula activity during exposure to smoking cues.
The meaning of this finding remains unclear, but it provides indirect evidence for a role of the insula in tobacco dependence.
